title: White Sox to host alumni home run derby headlined by José Canseco, Daniel Palka, Scott Podsednik
content:
Last summer, the Milwaukee Brewers held a postgame alumni home run derby in front of a sold-out crowd.

Now, the Chicago White Sox are copying the idea.

On July 11, the Sox will hold their own alumni home run derby, which will be part of a jam-packed day at Rate Field. The Sox have the No. 1 pick in the draft and are inviting fans to watch the selection before they play the A’s at 1:10 p.m. After that, the derby.

White Sox marketing guru Brooks Boyer said the team’s promotions committee seized on the concept last season and started the process of inviting former players earlier this year, once the team had set the date. Boyer is spinning it as a celebration of the franchise’s future, present and past, all on the same day.

But while the Brewers had Prince Fielder, Ryan Braun, Carlos Gómez and Corey Hart show up for last season’s exhibition, the Sox’s list, which was announced on Monday, is a bit less star-studded.

You won’t see Frank Thomas, Paul Konerko or Jim Thome. Still, fans will get a chance to gawk at the arms of José Canseco, who turns 62 nine days before the derby.

The favorite among the six-man field is probably Daniel Palka, the only participant to hit at least 25 homers in a season for the Sox. Twenty-seven of Palka’s 29 career home runs came in the 2018 season. He last played in Mexico in 2024.

“Palka can fall out of bed and hit,” Boyer said.

Former shortstop Alexei Ramírez hit 21 homers as a rookie with the Sox in 2008 and 109 during his eight seasons with the club. The 44-year-old Ramírez played for Cuba in the World Baseball Classic this spring and promptly tested positive for four anabolic steroids.

Also included in the field is Scott Podsednik, who famously hit zero home runs in the 2005 regular season and then hit two big ones in the playoffs that fall, including a walk-off homer against Houston Astros closer Brad Lidge in Game 2 of the World Series.

Leury García (34 homers in 676 games with the Sox) and Gordon Beckham (67 in 839 games for the Sox) round out the list of competitors.

Boyer and his staff reached out to several ex-Sox players who passed on the opportunity. Thome would’ve been interesting. He has been known to hit some BP dingers while coaching his son Landon’s high school in suburban Chicago, but he’s going to be busy that day with the draft — not only does he work in the Sox front office, but Landon Thome could be a hot commodity.

“There’s plenty of people that we inquired about, but it takes some guts to get up there in front of a big crowd and try to hit bombs,” Boyer said.

Beckham, who often fills in for Steve Stone in the Sox broadcast booth, said he needs to “lock it in” and start preparing. Despite not swinging a bat very often these days, the 39-year-old former infielder readily accepted the invite.

“I said ‘yes’ because my kids have never seen me do any baseball, and I thought they would have fun watching me,” he told The Athletic, adding that “finishing without a serious injury would be a win.”

While Boyer joked that he was making Beckham the favorite just to put pressure on him, the obvious star of the show, at least in terms of name recognition, is Canseco, the erstwhile Bash Brother who hit 462 homers in his roller-coaster career. Canseco’s final season in the majors was with the Sox in 2001, and he acquitted himself quite well, hitting 16 homers in 76 games.

Canseco’s last major-league home run came off Mike Mussina on Oct. 3, 2001, at Yankee Stadium. He then went on to a vagabond career in the independent leagues that ended in 2018.

“I don’t know if you’ve seen any of his videos recently,” Boyer said. “The guy looks in great shape, and you know he’ll probably grab like a 44-ounce bat and just hit tanks.”
